item.title: Where is the structure? — OK Movement questions NDC campaign council list
item.description: The Obi-Kwankwaso (OK) Movement has questioned the grassroots structure and preparedness of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) for the 2027 general elections following the party’s unveiling of its National Campaign Council. The Director-General of the OK Movement, John Ughulu, criticised the timing of the announcement, arguing that the party had delayed putting its campaign machinery in place and lacked the grassroots network required to prosecute a nationwide election. Ughulu stated this on Monday in a statement made available to journalists in Abuja, a day after the NDC announced the composition of its campaign council ahead of its inauguration in the Federal Capital Territory. He also boasted that the movement had established a stronger grassroots structure, predicting that some members of the newly announced council would eventually seek its support and mobilisation network. “The funny part of this list is that 90 per cent of the people on it will still come knocking on the doors of the OK Movement to beg for the very structure they have failed to build themselves!” he said. Ughulu further questioned the party’s readiness for the election, challenging its leadership to explain the delay in organising its campaign team. “With less than three months to the general elections, they are only just announcing their Presidential Campaign Council. What exactly have they been doing all this time? Where is the structure? Where is the strategy? Where is the machinery required to prosecute a serious national election?” he asked. The criticism comes amid an escalating disagreement between the NDC and the OK Movement over the movement’s organisational independence and its role in the campaign for the party’s presidential candidate, Peter Obi, and his running mate, Rabiu Kwankwaso. The NDC on Sunday announced its National Campaign Council, naming its National Leader, Senator Seriake Dickson, as chairman and Obi as co-chairman. The party’s National Chairman, Senator Cleopas Moses Zuwoghe, was appointed vice-chairman, while Kwankwaso was named co-vice-chairman. Other appointees include former Secretary to the Government of the Federation, Babachir Lawal, as chairman of the National Advisory Council; former Deputy Senate President, Senator Ovie Omo-Agege; former presidential candidate, Pat Utomi; and former National Secretary of the Congress for Progressive Change, Buba Galadima. The NDC National Secretary, Ikenna Enekweizu, was named council secretary, while Ibrahim Abdulkarim was appointed Director-General. Ughulu and the OK Movement’s state, local government and ward coordinators were not listed among the appointees. item.title: Gov Radda Pledges Sustained Investment As Katsina Records Decline In Malnutrition Cases
item.description: Katsina State Governor, Malam Dikko Umaru Radda, has reaffirmed his administration’s commitment to sustained investment in nutrition and healthcare, pledging to consolidate the significant progress recorded in reducing malnutrition across the state. Governor Radda gave the assurance on Sunday while receiving nutrition partners operating in Katsina State, led by the Executive Director of the Katsina State Development Management Board (KATDMB), Hajiya Ruqqaya Hamza, at the Government House, Katsina. The Governor said his administration would continue to prioritise nutrition as a critical component of human capital development, while calling on development partners to sustain technical assistance and institutional support to further strengthen the state’s healthcare and nutrition systems. He stressed the need for development organisations to align with the state’s recruitment policy by giving priority to qualified Katsina indigenes in the implementation of their programmes. According to him, building local capacity and integrating skilled professionals into government institutions remain essential for ensuring the long-term sustainability of development interventions. Governor Radda pointed to the Katsina State Development Management Board as an example of the success of such collaborations, noting that several of its personnel were beneficiaries of capacity-building initiatives supported by development partners. He encouraged the organisations to expand investments in human capital development to strengthen local institutions. Earlier, representatives of the nutrition partners presented updates on their interventions across the state during an interactive session. Governor Radda, on Sunday, October 25, 2026, while receiving nutrition partners operating in Katsina State, led by the Executive Director of the Katsina State Development Management Board (KATDMB), Hajiya Ruqqaya Hamza, at the Government House, Katsina. They reported a significant decline in malnutrition cases compared to the previous year, attributing the improvement to the Katsina State Government’s increased investment, strong leadership and unwavering political commitment to nutrition. The partners commended Governor Radda for placing nutrition high on the state’s development agenda and for committing substantial resources to the sector. They also called for deeper collaboration to sustain the gains already achieved and further improve nutrition outcomes across Katsina State. The meeting was attended by representatives of UNICEF, Médecins Sans Frontières (MSF), ALIMA, International Rescue Committee (IRC), JHPIEGO, Première Urgence Internationale (PUI), International Medical Corps (IMC), Médecins du Monde (MDM), Helen Keller International (HKI), Nutrition International, Save the Children/CGPP and Action Against Hunger. item.title: African players in Europe: Jackson brace ends City’s perfect record
item.description: Senegal star Nicolas Jackson took his goal tally since joining Aston Villa from Chelsea to seven in 11 matches by bagging a brace in a 2-1 Premier League win over Manchester City at the weekend. Victory for Villa ended a seven-match winning streak by City since the league season began. City still top the table, but only on goal difference from defending champions Arsenal. AFP Sport highlights African headline-makers in the major European leagues: ENGLAND NICOLAS JACKSON (Aston Villa) Jackson put Villa ahead in the sixth minute with a fine finish into the roof of the net from John McGinn’s pass. After Erling Haaland equalised for the leaders in the 52nd minute, Jackson clinched a memorable win for Villa eight minutes later. Teenage Senegal international Ibrahim Mbaye teed up Jackson to squeeze his shot past City goalkeeper Gianluigi Donnarumma. DANGO OUATTARA (Brentford) The Burkina Faso winger scored for the first time this season to rescue a 1-1 draw at Hull City. Ouattara slotted home in the 63rd minute from Igor Thiago’s pass. The 24-year-old cancelled out Oli McBurnie’s first half penalty, but Brentford were left without a win in their last three games. SPAIN INAKI WILLIAMS (Athletic Bilbao) After Spain 2026 World Cup winner Nico Williams came close to scoring, older brother and Ghana international Inaki struck the second goal in a 4-0 La Liga romp against Getafe. A counterattack ended with Inaki Williams one-on-one against the Getafe goalkeeper and he netted with a low shot. ITALY ANDRE-FRANK ANGUISSA (Napoli) Cameroon midfielder Anguissa sent a brilliant bicycle kick into the corner of the net on 28 minutes after Roma failed to clear a free-kick. It was the opening goal of a 3-3 Serie A thriller. GERMANY SERHOU GUIRASSY (Borussia Dortmund) Guirassy was kept off the scoresheet, but posed a constant threat as Borussia beat Eintracht Frankfurt 1-0 at home. Early in the opening half, the Guinea international was through on goal, but had his chip saved by goalkeeper Noah Atubolu. Just after the break, Guirassy headed a corner against the bar and went close again when he hit a cross inches wide of the left post. FRANCE ELYE WAHI, SOFIANE DIOP (Nice) Internationals Wahi of the Ivory Coast and Diop of Morocco scored as mid-table Nice came from behind to win 2-1 at Brest in Ligue 1. Wahi equalised just past the hour mark after a corner and Diop punished a defensive blunder to grab the 83rd-minute winner. item.title: Brazil’s Lula clinches poll victory, Bolsonaro seeks to annul election
item.description: Brazil’s leftist President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva pulled off a dramatic comeback on Sunday as he clinched a re-election victory, but his rival Flavio Bolsonaro refused to accept the loss and said he would seek to annul the vote. With Lula’s victory, Brazil staved off a conservative wave that has seen numerous countries — such as Argentina, Chile, Colombia, and Peru — all shift right, backed by US President Donald Trump. The leftist icon, who turns 81 on Tuesday, defied projections to win an unprecedented fourth term. According to official results, he won 51.8 percent of the votes to 48.2 percent for Flavio Bolsonaro, with Lula pulling around 4.4 million more votes. The senator is the son of former far-right president Jair Bolsonaro, who is serving a 27-year jail term for attempting a coup after his loss to Lula in the country’s last election in 2022. Sunday’s vote was marked by confusion after a Supreme Court ruling extended voting by two hours as some polling stations had already closed. The move came at the request of Lula who complained that buses had been pulled from circulation in various cities, barring citizens from voting. Flavio Bolsonaro also requested an extension in some regions due to heavy rains, but he described the decision as “unacceptable” and a “dirty trick” “It is impossible to recognize the results. I am going to request the annulment of these elections,” he said, stone-faced, in a brief speech in Brasilia. No candidate who lost the first round has gone on to win the second in Brazil since 1989, the first direct election after the end of the country’s military dictatorship. “People went to vote because we managed to convince them that voting was very important for ensuring democracy in the country,” Lula said in his first comments after the win. item.title: Vote For ‘Outstanding Warrior’ Netanyahu, Trump Tells Israelis

I would be a massive milestone in my career,” said the 33-year-old. But semi-final exits in both the Champions League and World Cup for Kane means the outcome is far from certain. “I think my wife would prefer to know and my family … it’s very stressful for everyone,” he added. “I can see why they don’t tell people. item.title: See Full List Of NDC Campaign Council Members
item.description: The Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) on Sunday released the list of its newly constituted national campaign council for the 2027 general elections. The list has Senator Seriake Dickson as the chairman, while the presidential candidate, Peter Obi, and vice-presidential candidate, Rabiu Musa Kwankwaso, were listed as co-chairman and co-vice chairman of the national campaign council, respectively. Others are Senator Cleopas Zuwoghe as vice chairman, and former secretary to the government of the federation, Babachir Lawal (National Campaign Advisory Council), as a member. Also on the list are Ikenna Enekweizu, Sidi Abdul, Babatunde Alli, Senator Ovie Omo Agege, Senator Victor Umeh, Ibrahim Abdulkarim (DG, Presidential Campaign), Buba Galadima, Yakubu Ochefu, Mahmud Jahun, Moshood Salvador, Mrs. Dudu Manuga, Victor Ogene, and Muktar Usman. The list also has a 40-member national campaign advisory council and 37 state campaign coordinators. The NDC National Publicity Secretary, Osa Director, was named Director of Communication and Media. A former defence spokesperson, Major General John Enenche (retd.), was named Director of Security and Intelligence. The party, in a statement announcing the campaign council on its X handle, said, “The Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) is pleased to announce the constitution of its National Campaign Council for the 2027 general elections. “The National Campaign Council will provide strategic leadership, coordinate campaign activities across the country, and drive the mobilisation of Nigerians behind the party’s vision of a new, just, and prosperous Nigeria. “The Council will work under the chairmanship of His Excellency, Senator Henry Seriake Dickson CON, NDC National Leader; Co-Chairman, His Excellency, Mr. Peter Obi CON, our presidential candidate; Vice Chairman, Senator Cleopas Moses Zuwoghe, NDC National Chairman and our vice-presidential candidate, His Excellency, Senator Rabiu Musa Kwankwaso, Co Vice-Chairman, Ikenna Morgan Enekweizu, NDC National Secretary, Council Secretary, and the Director-General, Mallam Ibrahim Hussain Abdulkarim to deliver a people-centred and issue-based campaign. “We call on all party members, supporters, and well-meaning Nigerians to remain united and focused as we work together to rescue our country.” See Full List Below: The post See Full List Of NDC Campaign Council Members appeared first on Channels Television .

They spoke on Sunday in Abuja at the 3rd Raymond Dokpesi Annual Diamond Lecture themed “Media, Democratic Consolidation and Development.” Uzodimma set the tone, urging government at all levels to stop treating the media as detractors or enemies. “Going forward, I propose a three-way pact between government, the media, and the citizens that will enable the media to drive national development,” he said. item.title: Dollar to Naira exchange rate today, October 26, 2026
item.description: The dollar is trading at different rates against the naira across Nigeria’s official foreign exchange market and the parallel market on Monday, October 26, 2026, with the latest available quotations showing differences between the two segments. At the Nigerian Foreign Exchange Market (NFEM), the official exchange rate was around ₦1,331 per dollar in the latest available market update, while parallel-market dealers quoted rates of approximately ₦1,370 to ₦1,385 per dollar, depending on the location and transaction. Data published by Gatekeepers News on Monday put the official dollar selling rate at ₦1,331.28, while the parallel market recorded a buying rate of ₦1,370 and a selling rate of ₦1,385 per dollar. However, exchange rates vary among banks, Bureau De Change (BDC) operators and other currency dealers, and the actual rate available to customers may differ from published indicative figures. The official foreign exchange market remains a key source of dollar pricing for eligible transactions conducted through authorised channels. The latest available figures for October 26 put the dollar at approximately ₦1,331 per dollar in the official market. This compares with the parallel market, where customers may pay more to purchase physical dollars. International currency data also showed movements in the dollar-naira pair on Monday, although such reference rates do not necessarily match the Central Bank of Nigeria’s official NFEM rate or the rates offered by local currency dealers. In the parallel market, currency dealers were quoting the dollar at approximately ₦1,370 for buying and ₦1,385 for selling, according to the latest market update published on Monday. The buying rate represents the amount dealers pay customers selling dollars, while the selling rate is the amount customers pay when purchasing the US currency. Based on these indicative quotations, $100 would be worth about ₦137,000 when sold to a dealer at the buying rate. Someone purchasing $100 at the selling rate would pay approximately ₦138,500. For $500, the equivalent would be ₦685,000 at the buying rate and ₦692,500 at the selling rate. Meanwhile, $1,000 would exchange for approximately ₦1,370,000 when sold to a dealer or cost ₦1,385,000 to purchase. These calculations are estimates based on published rates. Actual transactions may differ according to dealer pricing, location, dollar availability and the amount exchanged. Movements in the dollar-to-naira exchange rate affect Nigerian businesses and households that depend on imported goods and international payments. A higher dollar rate can increase the naira cost of imported raw materials, machinery, electronics and other products. Importers may consequently face higher operating expenses, which can feed into retail prices. Nigerians paying overseas tuition fees, medical bills and travel expenses also monitor exchange rates because changes in the value of the naira affect how much they need to pay for dollar-denominated transactions

item.title: Nigeria must manufacture meters locally, secure sustainable financing — Experts
item.description: By Esther Ihejirika Electricity sector experts have called for increased local meter manufacturing, sustainable financing and wider adoption of smart technology to accelerate meter deployment and close Nigeria’s metering gap. They made the call during a webinar on rapid meter rollout, stressing the need for a coordinated national metering plan to improve revenue collection, reduce estimated billing and curb electricity theft. Mr. Odion Omonfoman, host of the webinar, disclosed that the company had achieved “over 90 per cent metering coverage” and deployed more than 200,000 meters through the Meter Asset Provider (MAP) scheme and vendor-financing model. He said the company was targeting 100 per cent metering coverage by extending installations to all customers across its transformers and feeders. “Metering remains a strategic investment in revenue assurance. It enables customers to pay for the electricity they consume while reducing the dissatisfaction associated with estimated billing,” he said. Engr. Alegie Alfred, Head of Metering, Power Limited Electric Company (MPLEC), said Abia Power was tackling energy theft, meter bypass and vandalism through routine inspections, remote monitoring, consumption-pattern analysis, customer education and revenue-protection teams. Speaking on India’s experience, Ms. Ravleen Sethi, Director of Large Corporate Ratings, CareEdge, said government-backed programmes, private-sector investment and improved financing arrangements had accelerated smart-meter deployment in the country. She identified the Revamped Distribution Sector Scheme (RDSS), introduced in 2021, as a major driver of investment and expansion in India’s metering manufacturing capacity. From the manufacturing perspective, Engr. Durosola Omogbenigun, President, Meter Manufacturers Association of Nigeria, called for a national metering plan involving the Federal and state governments, electricity distribution companies, investors, regulators and local manufacturers. item.title: Domestic crude supply to refineries declines 6.3% to 15.97mb —NMDPRA
item.description: By Obas Esiedesa Domestic crude oil supply to Nigerian refineries declined by 6.3 per cent to 15.97 million barrels in September 2026 from 17.05 million barrels in August. This comes as petrol supply from domestic refineries and imports fell sharply during the month. The September 2026 Midstream and Downstream Report released by the Nigerian Midstream and Downstream Petroleum Regulatory Authority (NMDPRA) on Thursday shows that the decline in crude supply coincided with a 23.4 per cent drop in average daily petrol supply to 38.7 million litres from 50.5 million litres in August. The report attributed the fall in petrol receipts to lower domestic supply and reduced imports as approved import permit volumes were being exhausted. Between January and September 2026, refineries received a combined 156.51 million barrels of crude oil, comprising 125.85 million barrels of domestic crude and 30.66 million barrels of imported crude. Domestic production accounted for 80.4 per cent of total intake, while imported cargoes contributed 19.6 per cent. The report further showed that Dangote Refinery’s utilisation stood at 105.98 per cent in September, implying crude processing of approximately 689,000 barrels per day against average crude receipts of 618,000 barrels per day. The difference of about 71,000 barrels per day was drawn from refinery inventory, indicating that the refinery processed more crude than it received during the month. Despite the September decline, domestic refineries remained the larger source of petrol supply, accounting for approximately 73.6 per cent of total receipts during the month, compared with 26.4 per cent from imports. The September total was also below the 13-month average of 49.7 million litres per day recorded between September 2025 and September 2026. Over the 13-month period, domestic refineries supplied an average of 30.4 million litres per day, accounting for 61.2 per cent of total supply, while imports contributed 19.3 million litres per day, or 38.8 per cent. The NMDPRA said September petrol receipts declined as domestic supply fell 21 per cent below August levels, while imports dropped by 30 per cent amid the exhaustion of approved import permit volumes. item.title: Stock market extend losses, 55 stocks depreciate
item.description: …As 20 record capital gains By Peter Egwuatu Share prices of 55 companies listed on the Nigerian Exchange Limited (NGX) depreciated last week following profit taking by the investors. However, 20 stocks appreciated in price during the week under review. The week’s performance highlights the market correction facing the stock market as investors reassess their portfolios following the substantial gains recorded earlier in the year. Although selected stocks attracted buying interest, the recovery was not broad enough to offset losses in influential stocks, leaving the overall market sentiment negative. Analysts emphasised that the decline also came against the backdrop of rising international oil prices, which climbed sharply amid escalating geopolitical tensions in the Middle East. While higher crude prices could support Nigeria’s export earnings and government revenue, their broader implications for domestic fuel costs, inflation and business expenses remain important considerations for investors. A review of the market performance last week showed that the NGX market capitalisation, which represents the total value of stocks, shed over N206 billion to close at N160.519 trillion from N160.725 trillion the previous week. In similar manner, the NGX All Share Index, ASI, close lower to 247,222.27 points from 247539.73 points. Meanwhile, a total turnover of 2.024 billion shares worth N110.773 billion in 173,113 deals was traded last week by investors on the floor of the Exchange, in contrast to a total of 1.659 billion shares valued at N98.088 billion that exchanged hands the previous week in 184,632 deals. The Financial Services Industry (measured by volume) led the activity chart with 1.111 billion shares valued at N53.908 billion traded in 81,787 deals: thus contributing 54.89% and 48.66% to the total equity turnover volume and value respectively. The Consumer Goods Industry followed with 394.039 million shares worth N9.811 billion in 17,912 deals. Third place was the Agriculture Industry, with a turnover of 147.170 million shares worth N2.821 billion in 7,462 deals. Analysing market performance and outlook, analysts at InvestData Consulting Limited, stated: “The near-term outlook for the Nigerian equities market remains cautious as investors balance the need to preserve gains against opportunities in selected stocks. The market’s substantial year-to-date appreciation provides important context for the recent weakness, as some participants may be reducing exposure after the strong returns accumulated earlier in the year. Continued selling pressure in banking, energy and other influential stocks could prolong the market’s consolidation. Further weakness in large capitalised stocks may continue to weigh on the benchmark even if selected equities record positive returns.” The post Stock market extend losses, 55 stocks depreciate appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Soldiers earn peanuts, APC youth leader flaunts billion-naira SUVs — Utomi
item.description: Professor Pat Utomi has criticised the All Progressives Congress (APC) over the distribution of luxury sport utility vehicles (SUVs) to selected youth leaders, contrasting the expenditure with what he described as poor salaries paid to Nigerian soldiers. Utomi, a chieftain of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC), said it was troubling that an APC youth leader could display expensive vehicles at a time Nigerians had been told that government funds were limited. In a post on X on Sunday, Utomi wrote: “Nigerian soldiers are being paid peanuts as salaries, yet an APC youth leader is flaunting SUVs worth billions of naira. This is the same government that told Nigerians there was no longer money in the treasury. At this point, they must think we are fools!” In another post, the professor questioned whether the money spent on the vehicles could have been put to better use, particularly in the health sector. “Each of the SUVs in this video costs more than ₦100 million. I wonder how many world-class ambulances the millions being spent on these vehicles could buy. What a pity!” he wrote. The comments followed a video posted by APC National Youth Leader, Dayo Israel, showing brand-new 2026 Toyota Prado SUVs he said were presented to selected youth leaders to support election mobilisation ahead of the 2027 general elections. “Today, I presented brand new 2026 Prado to my committed selected youth leaders to aid their election mobilisation activities,” Israel wrote. He also expressed gratitude to First Lady Oluremi Tinubu for what he described as her continued support for the party’s structure under his leadership. “The party is supreme and that supremacy will show in our action in this election period — we will deliver polling unit by polling unit,” he added. The video, which has since been deleted, drew criticism from Nigerians on social media, with some questioning the timing of the vehicle distribution amid the economic hardship associated with the Tinubu administration’s reforms. Utomi’s remarks add to the criticism surrounding the display, with the NDC chieftain raising questions about public spending priorities and the cost of the vehicles. item.title: ‘We are not bandits’ – Herdsmen; want 30% of agric budget, 417 grazing reserves
item.description: By Omeiza Ajayi, ABUJA Pastoralist groups have rejected the profiling of Fulani pastoralists as bandits and called on President Bola Tinubu to immediately declare a national dialogue on farmer-herder conflicts, following what they say are the killings of hundreds of pastoralists in recent months. At a news conference on Sunday in Abuja, President of Kautal Pulaaku Fulbe Association of Nigeria, Dr. Huseini Buzaye, who signed an address on behalf of the Confederation of Pastoralist Non-Governmental Organisations CONPA, said the groups represent “millions of Nigerian pastoralists from all 36 states and FCT”, under over 30 associations. General Secretary of the association, Abdullahi Ardo, who read the prepared speech on behalf of the president, said; “For too long, the word ‘Fulani Pastoralist’ has been profiled and criminalized as synonymous with banditry, kidnapping and terrorism”. The groups said the stereotyping “has given impetus to jungle justice, extrajudicial killings, and hate speech against innocent pastoralists, including women and children who have no connection to crime.” “Criminals are criminals and have no tribe,” the statement said, urging security agencies and the media to “stop ethnic profiling but arrest and prosecute criminals as individuals, not as an ethnic group”, they added. On the killings, the coalition said in the last few months, hundreds of innocent pastoralists have been killed in coordinated attacks in Plateau, Niger, Sokoto, Kebbi, Zamfara and other parts of the country. It said women, children and the elderly were among the dead, thousands of cattle were rustled or killed, and entire Rugas were burnt down. “These killings are not reported. There is no national outrage. There is no compensation. There is no justice,” it said. The groups demanded an independent investigation into the killings. item.content:encoded: By Omeiza Ajayi, ABUJA Pastoralist groups have rejected the profiling of Fulani pastoralists as bandits and called on President Bola Tinubu to immediately declare a national dialogue on farmer-herder conflicts, following what they say are the killings of hundreds of pastoralists in recent months. At a news conference on Sunday in Abuja, President of Kautal Pulaaku Fulbe Association of Nigeria, Dr. Huseini Buzaye, who signed an address on behalf of the Confederation of Pastoralist Non-Governmental Organisations CONPA, said the groups represent “millions of Nigerian pastoralists from all 36 states and FCT”, under over 30 associations. General Secretary of the association, Abdullahi Ardo, who read the prepared speech on behalf of the president, said; “For too long, the word ‘Fulani Pastoralist’ has been profiled and criminalized as synonymous with banditry, kidnapping and terrorism”. The groups said the stereotyping “has given impetus to jungle justice, extrajudicial killings, and hate speech against innocent pastoralists, including women and children who have no connection to crime.” “Criminals are criminals and have no tribe,” the statement said, urging security agencies and the media to “stop ethnic profiling but arrest and prosecute criminals as individuals, not as an ethnic group”, they added. On the killings, the coalition said in the last few months, hundreds of innocent pastoralists have been killed in coordinated attacks in Plateau, Niger, Sokoto, Kebbi, Zamfara and other parts of the country. It said women, children and the elderly were among the dead, thousands of cattle were rustled or killed, and entire Rugas were burnt down. “These killings are not reported. There is no national outrage. There is no compensation. There is no justice,” it said. The groups demanded an independent investigation into the killings. They also asked the Federal Government to direct the National Emergency Management Agency NEMA and the National Commission for Refugees, Migrants and Internally Displaced Persons NCFRMI to provide relief materials to displaced pastoralists “as it does for other communities”. They also asked security agencies to protect pastoralists “as Nigerian citizens under Section 14 and Section 33 of the 1999 Constitution.” The coalition commended Tinubu for creating the Federal Ministry of Livestock Development, calling it “a historic decision that gave us hope after 60 years of agitation.” But it said the ministry “remains largely unfunded and without a clear operational framework” years after its creation. It appealed for the ministry “to be seen active at the community level”, and asked the President and the National Assembly to allocate at least 30 per cent of the agricultural budget to it, to “immediately gazette and protect the 417 grazing reserves”, and to start pilot ranches and fodder production in the six geo-political zones. “Livestock is a 30 trillion economy. It cannot be treated with levity,” the statement said. Citing what it described as more than 20,000 deaths from the farmer-herder conflict in 10 years, the coalition said: “Nigeria cannot achieve peace by military means alone.” It called on the President to make “a Presidential Declaration of National Dialogue and Reconciliation on Farmer-Herder and Pastoralist Conflicts”. It said the dialogue should include Miyetti Allah groups, traditional rulers, the Christian Association of Nigeria CAN, Jama’atu Nasril Islam JNI, security agencies and state governments, with a mandate of “Truth, Justice, Forgiveness, Compensation, and a Roadmap for Peaceful Co-existence.” The groups also listed responsibilities for pastoralist communities, urging leaders, households and young people to respect farmers’ rights and lawful property, take “reasonable measures to prevent livestock from entering cultivated farmland”, and cooperate with lawful security investigations. They urged them to report cattle rustling and kidnapping, and to reject violence, banditry and retaliatory violence. The coalition said it intends to carry out mass awareness and sensitisation across the six geo-political zones, with a framework already worked out. “We are Nigerians. We are pastoralists. We are not bandits. We love this country. Our cattle feed this nation,” the statement said. item.title: IPoB alleges secret transfer of 68 detainees
item.description: By Steve Oko UMUAHIA—The Indigenous People of Biafra, IPoB, has alleged that 68 detained Biafrans were secretly transferred from Wawa Barracks to correctional facilities in Kuje, Keffi and Suleja, accusing the Federal Government of using the justice system to prolong the detention of its members. The group also alleged that the Court of Appeal had yet to list an appeal challenging the conviction of its leader, Mazi Nnamdi Kanu, despite the compilation and transmission of the record of appeal. IPOB made the allegations in its weekly address issued on Sunday by the Head of its Directorate of State, DOS, Mazi Chris Nwaogu. Nwaogu said the group’s legal team had identified the 68 detainees and was working to secure their release. He urged supporters to sustain legal efforts on behalf of those in custody. He further alleged that a separate fundamental rights suit concerning Kanu’s detention had suffered a setback after the presiding judge reportedly announced that the court file was missing. According to him, the suit concerns Kanu’s detention for 14 months following his discharge by the Court of Appeal on October 13, 2022. The IPOB spokesman also challenged the legal basis of Kanu’s conviction by Justice Omotosho on November 20, 2025, alleging that the judgment relied on a repealed law. He cited Section 36(12) of the Constitution, which provides that a person cannot be convicted of a criminal offence unless the offence and its penalty are prescribed in written law. Meanwhile, IPOB disowned an audio message circulating online that purportedly announced the return of an enforced Monday sit-at-home across the South-East. Nwaọgụ said neither the DOS nor the High Command of the Eastern Security Network, ESN, had authorised the action, warning against attempts to enforce an unauthorised shutdown. He urged residents to disregard the message and avoid actions capable of provoking violence or disrupting economic activities in the region. The group also announced what it described as a phased political disengagement, directing its supporters to boycott activities associated with the All Progressives Congress, APC, ahead of the 2027 general elections. It urged supporters to stay away from APC rallies, stop carrying the party’s flags and refrain from defending APC governors, while maintaining its position on boycotting the 2027 elections. Nwaọgụ said the proposed boycott was a response to what the group described as injustice, unlawful detention and persecution of its members. He, however, cautioned supporters against violence and warned politicians against hijacking the planned boycott for their own interests. IPOB reiterated its demand for Kanu’s immediate and unconditional release, urging the judiciary to list the appeal for hearing and determine the legal issues surrounding his conviction. item.description: By Peter Egwuatu Share prices of 55 companies listed on the Nigerian Exchange Limited (NGX) depreciated last week following profit taking by the investors. However, 20 stocks appreciated in price during the week under review. The week’s performance highlights the market correction facing the stock market as investors reassess their portfolios following the substantial gains recorded earlier in the year. Although selected stocks attracted buying interest, the recovery was not broad enough to offset losses in influential stocks, leaving the overall market sentiment negative. Analysts emphasised that the decline also came against the backdrop of rising international oil prices, which climbed sharply amid escalating geopolitical tensions in the Middle East. While higher crude prices could support Nigeria’s export earnings and government revenue, their broader implications for domestic fuel costs, inflation and business expenses remain important considerations for investors. A review of the market performance last week showed that the NGX market capitalisation, which represents the total value of stocks, shed over N206 billion to close at N160.519 trillion from N160.725 trillion the previous week. In similar manner, the NGX All Share Index, ASI, close lower to 247,222.27 points from 247539.73 points. Meanwhile, a total turnover of 2.024 billion shares worth N110.773 billion in 173,113 deals was traded last week by investors on the floor of the Exchange, in contrast to a total of 1.659 billion shares valued at N98.088 billion that exchanged hands the previous week in 184,632 deals. The Financial Services Industry (measured by volume) led the activity chart with 1.111 billion shares valued at N53.908 billion traded in 81,787 deals: thus contributing 54.89% and 48.66% to the total equity turnover volume and value respectively. The Consumer Goods Industry followed with 394.039 million shares worth N9.811 billion in 17,912 deals. Third place was the Agriculture Industry, with a turnover of 147.170 million shares worth N2.821 billion in 7,462 deals. Analysing market performance and outlook, analysts at InvestData Consulting Limited, stated: “The near-term outlook for the Nigerian equities market remains cautious as investors balance the need to preserve gains against opportunities in selected stocks. The market’s substantial year-to-date appreciation provides important context for the recent weakness, as some participants may be reducing exposure after the strong returns accumulated earlier in the year. Continued selling pressure in banking, energy and other influential stocks could prolong the market’s consolidation. Further weakness in large capitalised stocks may continue to weigh on the benchmark even if selected equities record positive returns.” Vanguard News The post Stock market extend losses, 55 stocks depreciate; 20 record capital gains appeared first on Vanguard News .
